SecureKeys cuts a strong password from a passphrase you can remember, the same one every time. Nothing is stored.
SecureKeys works fully offline and shows no ads. It doesn\'t even ask for internet access, so your passphrase never leaves this device.
The Archivo and Martian Mono typefaces are used under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
SecureKeys turns a passphrase you can remember into a strong password. The same passphrase and settings always give the same password, so nothing needs to be stored. It takes four steps:

string-array.name: help_steps
string-array.item: Enter a passphrase of your choice. Something you can remember easily.
Choose the length of the password you want generated.
Choose the types of characters you want in your generated password.
Tap Generate password, then tap the key to copy it.

string-array.name: help_tips
string-array.item: Do not use the same password for multiple important accounts.
Use a password that has at least 15 characters, with at least one number, one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter and one special symbol.
Do not use the names of your family, friends or pets in your passwords.
Do not use postcodes, house numbers, phone numbers, birthdates, ID card numbers, social security numbers and so on in your passwords.
Do not use any dictionary word in your passwords.
Do not let your web browsers store your passwords, since passwords saved in browsers can be revealed easily.
Do not log in to important accounts on computers of others, or when connected to a public Wi-Fi hotspot, Tor, a free VPN or a web proxy.
Remember a few master passwords and store the others in a file encrypted with 7-Zip, GPG or a disk-encryption tool such as BitLocker, or use a password manager.
Turn on two-step authentication whenever possible.
Do not store your critical passwords in the cloud.
